title: An algebraic zero-dimensional scheme over a field is affine and finite
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $\dim Y\le0$ [def-pc-dimension]. Then $Y$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], and the structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] the Krull dimension of the underlying topological space of Y [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equals $\sup_{y\in Y}\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, which is $\dim Y$ in the sense of [def-pc-dimension] (both are $-\infty$ if Y is empty); so the topological dimension of Y is at most 0. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] to the finite-type morphism Y to Spec k and this topological hypothesis. It gives that the underlying topological space of Y is finite and discrete.
A scheme with finite discrete underlying space is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine]. Thus Y is affine; write Y = Spec B with B = Gamma(Y, O_Y).

Since the original structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type and Y is affine, [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] says that the induced k-algebra B is of finite type. If Y is empty then B = 0 has no primes. Otherwise apply [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] to the one-member cover of Y by Y = Spec B: the Krull dimension of the ring B equals dim Y <= 0, so there is no strict inclusion of primes of B, i.e. every prime of B is maximal.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-dim-zero-finite] to B. It gives that B is finite-dimensional over k. Therefore the affine structure morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, since a finite-dimensional k-algebra is a finite k-algebra.
